the existence of a cluster is explained by the presence of knowledge-based economies, and that the internal organization of the cluster is explained by its ability to facilitate the creation and transfer of knowledge.
the cluster is a knowledge creation system, and that the knowledge creation process is the driving force for the existence and internal organization of the cluster.
the cluster is a knowledge-creation mechanism and that the cluster can be viewed as an organizational arrangement for the purpose of knowledge creation.

two issues: (i) the existence of a cluster and its boundaries, (ii) the nature of the internal organization of the cluster.

the cluster is an organization of firms, which are engaged in knowledge-creation activities and are located in close proximity to each other in order to benefit from a number of advantages related to knowledge spillovers.
the cluster is a complex phenomenon that is not well understood.
the cluster is an important source of knowledge spillovers, and therefore, of innovation.

we have tried to provide a framework for a theory of the knowledge-based cluster.
a theory of the knowledge-based cluster should be based on a theory of the firm.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the concept of the cluster should be seen as an emergent phenomenon, which cannot be explained by the mere aggregation of its individual components.

the cluster is a knowledge-based phenomenon, and that it is the interaction of the various agents within the cluster that is the main source of knowledge spillovers and the main driver of cluster dynamics.
